title: Invited: Achieving PetaOps/W Edge-AI Processing
problem: Edge AI processing requires massive improvements in energy efficiency to enable deployment on edge devices for sensing applications. Current cloud-based AI approaches lack the power budget needed to move inference to resource-constrained edge devices.
motivation: Deploying AI processing to edge devices would enable real-time inference with improved latency, privacy, and reduced cloud dependency.
method: The CONVOLVE project optimizes energy across the full computing stack for edge AI. It uses Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs)—brain-inspired models that use sparse events instead of continuous values—combined with compute-in-memory (CIM) architectures that process data where it's stored, reducing power-hungry data movement. The hardware uses memristor-based devices (components that perform analog computation) and approximation techniques (low-precision math to save energy). To handle hardware imperfections, it employs online continuous learning—adapting weights during operation to compensate for noise and variations.
key_novelty: The core innovation is combining online continuous learning with compute-in-memory architectures, enabling edge AI systems to self-adapt and tolerate imperfections in analog hardware.
contributions: CIM (compute-in-memory) architecture designs for energy-efficient neural network execution
SNN accelerators optimized for ultra-low-power edge AI inference
Online learning techniques for real-time weight adaptation and noise tolerance
Holistic cross-layer design approach spanning models, mappings, processing architectures, and device technology
limitations: Specific quantitative performance results, baseline comparisons, and detailed evaluation methodology are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Energy-efficient edge AI through cross-layer design stack optimization
